phases.name: Foundation -- Agent Contracts and Data Models

steps.name: Agent JSON output contracts and Pydantic models
steps.description: Define Pydantic models for all 6 agent JSON schemas. These are the integration contracts that agents must conform to and the normalizer consumes.
criteria: Each of the 6 agents has a corresponding Pydantic model
Models validate required fields, types, and value ranges
Invalid JSON produces clear error identifying the agent and field
Models are frozen (immutable)

steps.name: Report data structures and overall score model
steps.description: Define the unified report data structure: metadata, normalized dimension scores, overall health score, rating, business risk assessments.
criteria: Report data model includes metadata, dimension scores, overall score, risk assessments
Overall score computable from dimension scores via documented formula
Rating derivable from overall score via threshold lookup
Missing dimensions representable (optional fields)

steps.name: Score normalization functions
steps.description: Pure functions that transform raw agent JSON (validated by models) into normalized 0-10 dimension scores using the documented formulas.
criteria: Each agent type has a normalization function
Output scores are in 0-10 range
Applying the formula to known input reproduces expected output
Functions return both the normalized score and the formula-with-values string

steps.name: Overall health score and business risk derivation
steps.description: Pure functions for weighted health score calculation (0-100) and business risk category assessment (Delivery Velocity, Incident, Onboarding).
criteria: Health score is weighted average of available dimensions, scaled to 0-100
Missing dimensions cause weight redistribution (not score penalty)
Each risk category produces severity level (HIGH/MODERATE/LOW) and contributing dimension citations
All-healthy dimensions produce LOW across all risk categories

steps.name: HTML base template with inlined libraries and navigation
steps.description: Jinja2 base template containing the HTML skeleton, inlined Chart.js/D3.js/Mermaid.js, sticky navigation bar, print CSS, and report data injection point.
criteria: Single HTML file renders in modern browser with no external dependencies
Sticky navigation bar with section links is present
Print CSS hides interactive elements and produces clean output
Report data injectable as const reportData = {...} in script tag

steps.name: Executive summary section with radar chart and gauges
steps.description: Jinja2 template section rendering overall health gauge, 6-axis radar chart, dimension score bars, weakest dimension callout, and business risk summary.
criteria: Overall score displayed as gauge with rating label
Radar chart renders with correct axis labels and data points
Weakest dimension visually highlighted with risk annotation
Business risk categories displayed with severity badges
Executive summary scannable in under 2 minutes on standard display

steps.name: Score derivation panels and dimension detail sections
steps.description: Reusable Jinja2 template for per-dimension detail: score derivation, dimension-specific charts, and findings tables. Render once per available dimension.
criteria: Each dimension has a detail section accessible from executive summary
Score derivation shows raw data, formula with substituted values, and plain-language explanation
Applying displayed formula to displayed data reproduces displayed score
Failed dimensions show Not Available with reason
Navigation between executive summary and dimension sections is bidirectional

steps.name: Python pipeline entry point
steps.description: Single Python function that reads agent JSON files from a directory, runs normalization, derives risks, assembles report data, renders templates, and writes the HTML file.
criteria: Given a directory of valid agent JSON files, produces a valid HTML report
Handles partial results (missing agent files) without error
Reports which agents were available and which were missing
Exit code 0 on success, non-zero on fatal error (e.g., no agents at all)

steps.name: Orchestrator agent definition
steps.description: Claude Code agent markdown file that validates target directory, launches 6 subagents (5 parallel + 1 sequential), handles failures, then invokes the Python pipeline.
criteria: Agent accepts target directory and optional config (project name, output path, agent selection)
Independent agents launch without waiting for each other
Refactoring agent waits for code smell detector to complete
Agent failure is caught and reported; remaining agents continue
Python pipeline invoked after all agents complete (or fail)

steps.name: Add JSON output to all 6 analysis agents
steps.description: Modify each agent's .md definition at /Users/andrealaforgia/dev/claude-code-agents/ to write a {agent-name}-data.json file conforming to the defined contract schemas.
criteria: Each agent writes a valid JSON file alongside its markdown report
JSON conforms to the Pydantic model for that agent
DDD and legacy agents include a self-assessed 0-10 overall score with rubric justification
Existing agent behavior and markdown output is unchanged
